title: Unified fallback signal unifier and hysteresis orchestrator for region/tier routing
creator: Anjali Rao
description:
Problem: When regional capacity pressure, transient spikes, or noisy upstream models occur we need deterministic, safe automatic fallback behavior that avoids flip-flopping and minimizes user-visible errors. Current mechanisms respond to single signals (e.g., 429s or latency) in isolation which leads to premature or delayed fallbacks and inconsistent behavior across tenants and routes.

Goal: Design and implement a unified signal unifier + hysteresis orchestrator that: 1) aggregates multiple signals (429s, client timeouts, service errors, p99 latency spikes, sustained queue depth) into a single trip score per route/tenant/region/tier; 2) supports configurable weighting and per-tenant sensitivity; 3) enforces exponential hysteresis (graceful escalation + cooldown) to avoid oscillation; 4) provides observability, simulation harness, and a safe canary rollout path with automatic rollback.

Key design points: 
- Signals to include: HTTP 429 and 503 rates, upstream model error-rate (model-specific error codes), timeout count, p95/p99 latency deltas vs baseline, queue utilization, sustained token generation stalls, and explicit runtime backpressure signals.
- Sliding windows: short window Ws=30s for burst detection, medium Wm=5m for persistent pressure, long Wl=30m for trend detection. TripScore = sum_i (w_i * normalized(signal_i, window)) where normalization maps each raw signal into [0,1] relative to dynamic baselines.
- Thresholding: two thresholds T_warn and T_trip. T_warn triggers internal routing alternatives and increased telemetry; T_trip triggers fallback to lower-cost/compatible model variant or regional failover. Both thresholds are tunable per route and per tenant.
- Hysteresis: when TripScore crosses T_trip we enter a degraded state for a min_hold (default 60s) then apply exponentially increasing hold windows on repeated toggles (min_hold * backoff_factor^n). Recovery requires TripScore to fall below T_recover = T_trip * 0.6 for a sustained window of Wm.
- Circuit state machine: CLOSED -> WARNING -> OPEN -> BACKOFF -> PROBING. PROBING sends a small percentage of traffic to primary to test recovery with fast metrics evaluation.
- Per-tenant sensitivity: enterprise tenants can set more conservative thresholds and shorter probes; freemium tiers can have more aggressive fallback.
- Compatibility and fallback actions: (a) model variant fallback (quantized/low-latency variant), (b) region reroute, (c) route-specified static fallback response, (d) queued retry with jitter. Fallback action chosen by policy priority and compatibility matrix.
- Observability: new metrics: trips_by_route, trip_score_distribution, trips_by_signal, probe_success_rate, average_hold_duration. Dashboards in Console + per-tenant audit logs for fallback decisions.
- Simulation & validation: offline replay harness that feeds production traffic traces through the TripScore calculator and outputs false-positive/false-negative rates vs current incidents.

Trade-offs and rationale: 
- Aggregating multiple noisy signals reduces bad fallbacks due to single-signal noise but requires careful normalization to avoid dominant signals drowning others. We favor dynamic baselines and adaptive normalization tied to historical percentiles to mitigate seasonality.
- Exponential hysteresis increases time-to-recover for repeated flaps but drastically reduces oscillation; we mitigate long recoveries via targeted PROBING.
- Per-tenant config surface increases complexity but is necessary for enterprise SLAs; default safe profiles for most users will minimize ops burden.

Open decisions: 
- Default signal weights (proposal below) vs fully adaptive learned weighting.
- Storage/backing of per-tenant thresholds: config service vs code-defined defaults.
- Whether to expose trip_score raw value to users or only action/audit logs.

Proposed default weights (initial): 429_rate: 0.35, timeout_rate: 0.25, service_error_rate(5xx): 0.15, p99_latency_delta: 0.15, queue_utilization: 0.05, token_stall: 0.05.

Compatibility with existing features: must interoperate with routing policies (regional priority), quota enforcement, Dedicated capacity routing, and Optimize suggestions. Fall back actions must consult model compatibility matrix to ensure variant supports same API.

Rollout plan (high level): design -> simulation -> small canary (1% global routes) with PROBING disabled -> expand to 10% with PROBING enabled -> tenant opt-in for enterprise -> global. Auto-rollback triggers if probe_success_rate < 80% or false_trip_rate > 1% on canary traces.
acceptance_criteria: Signal unifier implemented as a standalone service/library with stable API (tripScore(route, windowConfig) -> float)
Default weights and thresholds implementable via runtime config toggles without code deploys
Hysteresis state machine implemented with exponential backoff and PROBING state
Simulation harness exists and shows reduced false-positive fallback rate vs today on two week production replay (target: >=40% reduction)
End-to-end canary executed and dashboard shows trip metrics, and an automatic rollback hook is in place
Per-route and per-tenant audit logs emitted for every fallback decision
Unit and integration tests cover normalization logic, state transitions, and probe behavior
